context:
Owner decision 2026-11-20 (choice dialog): "approve this run list. I bring you the table before any estimate figure is committed." ('I' is the agent.) Run list: `dsqgen` all 99 queries at SF 1, 100, 1000, 3000, 5000; `dsdgen` and `dbgen` full generation at SF 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10 (SF 10 writes about 10 GB each); on this Mac, one at a time through `make heavy-run`. Also from the dialog: "With the estimate in place, a run warns when `--timeout` is shorter than the estimate." Worked after the five run-timeout steps; needs step 1 for the warning. Run folders under ~/Developer/benchmark_runs are kept.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
The agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. Arming: `make pr-arm` once; one more attempt only when the refusal named a cause, the agent reported it and the cause is cleared; never a third without asking; `make pr-rerun` at most once and only for a job that never ran or was cancelled by the runner, never for a test that failed. Review threads: reply, and resolve only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise the finding again. Subagents are read-only. Any limit, default, threshold or label text the owner has not already chosen is shown to the owner before it is committed. No file edit by script; use the edit tool. Do not edit a pull request description while its CI is starting; post a comment. A blocked step stops this item; no workaround. No live cloud run. Heavy work only through `make heavy-run`.
description:
## Problem
A user starting TPC data or query generation at a large scale has no idea how long it will take. The only estimate shown today is a per-benchmark minutes range in the interactive prompt, which does not vary with scale.

## Owner decisions, 2026-11-20
"We should also provide a rough estimate for the user about expected duration". Chosen option: "Recommended: measure first. Run dsdgen and dsqgen at a few scales through make heavy-run (I bring you the list and the table), then print an estimate before generation that is labelled rough and names the scales it was measured at."

## Change
First bring the owner the list of measurement runs (tool, benchmark, scales, expected disk and memory, host). After approval, run them through `make heavy-run` and bring the table. Then print an estimate before generation, labelled rough, naming the scales and host class it was measured on.

## Decision gates
No measurement run before the owner approves the list. No estimate figure is committed before the owner has seen the table. Known so far, darwin-arm64 only: dsqgen query 9 about 5 s at SF 3000 and 11 to 13 s at SF 5000; nothing larger completed; no dsdgen durations by scale are in hand.

## Verification rubric
Pass: the approved run list and the measured table are recorded here with heavy-run log paths; the printed estimate for a measured scale is within the measured range, and for an unmeasured scale it says it is extrapolated; a test covers both.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
Accepted by the owner in the choice dialog: the agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. It arms with `make pr-arm` once per pull request and reports the result. Subagents are read-only. Any limit, default, threshold or label text is shown to the owner before it is committed. A blocked step stops this item; the agent moves to the next item and does not work around the block.
Review threads: the accepted text also said the agent never resolves a thread. Asked afterwards which rule applies, the owner chose: "The morning rule: I may resolve a thread once the bot has reviewed the new head and did not raise the finding again." ('I' is the agent.) So the agent pushes the fix and replies, and resolves a thread only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise that finding again.
